    // The character at index n. Precondition: 0 <= n < Count; outside it the call faults
    // (the C# runtime throws IndexOutOfRangeException, the interpreter an evaluation
    // error, the C++ prelude asserts), so test the index first. A Character is one UTF-16
    // code unit in C# and the interpreter and one byte in the C++ prelude, identical for
    // the Latin-1 text the STEP parser reads. Witness: "abc".At(1).ToInteger == 98.
    At(s: String, n: Integer): Character;

    // The code unit value of the character: 97 for a. Witness: "a".At(0).ToInteger == 97.
    ToInteger(self: Character): Integer;

    // The character with that code unit value (the low 16 bits in C#, the low 8 in the C++
    // prelude; 0 to 255 agree everywhere). With FromCharacters this builds any text,
    // including the line feed (10) and carriage return (13) a Plato literal cannot hold.
    // Witness: 97.ToCharacter.ToInteger == 97 and FromCharacters([10.ToCharacter]).Count == 1.
    ToCharacter(self: Integer): Character;

    // The characters at the indices start to start + count - 1 that exist. The range
    // is clamped to the String at both ends, so a negative start, a count past the end,
    // a count of zero or less, and a range wholly outside never fail: the last two give
    // "". Expressible as FromCharacters over MapRange and At, but that copies and
    // allocates once per character and the STEP parser slices every keyword; the
    // intrinsic is one block copy. Witness: Substring("abcd", 1, 2) == "bc";
    // Substring("abcd", -1, 3) == "ab" and Substring("abcd", 3, 9) == "d".
    Substring(s: String, start: Integer, count: Integer): String;

    // Whether the text is a number in the P21 real forms: an optional sign, digits with
    // an optional point and more digits (at least one digit in all), then an optional
    // exponent E or e with an optional sign and digits. "1.", ".5" and "1.E-06" are
    // numbers. Anything else is not: "", ".", "1e", "NaN", "Infinity", "0x10", " 1", and
    // a text whose value rounds to infinity ("1e999"). The form is checked by hand so
    // that every runtime agrees on it; ParseNumber in text.library.plato pairs this with
    // NumberFromText. Witness: IsNumberText("1.E-06") and not IsNumberText("1e").
    IsNumberText(s: String): Boolean;

    // The value of the number the text spells, correctly rounded to the nearest Number by
    // the host's own parser (double.Parse in the invariant culture, std::from_chars in
    // C++), so the runtimes agree bit for bit; "-0" is negative zero. 0 when IsNumberText
    // is false. Not expressible in Plato: it is a correctly rounded decimal-to-binary
    // conversion, which needs the host's big-integer path or a table of powers.
    // Witness: NumberFromText("1.5E1") == 15.0 and NumberFromText("abc") == 0.0.
    NumberFromText(s: String): Number;

    // Whether the text is an optional sign and one or more decimal digits whose value fits
    // Integer under the profile (64-bit under cpu64, 32-bit under cpu64i32 and gpu32).
    // "-0", "+7" and "007" are integers. "", "+", "1.0", "1e3", " 1" and a value past the
    // range are not: overflow is reported, never wrapped. Pairs with IntegerFromText in
    // ParseInteger (text.library.plato). Witness: IsIntegerText("-12") and not
    // IsIntegerText("99999999999999999999").
    IsIntegerText(s: String): Boolean;

    // The Integer the text spells; 0 when IsIntegerText is false. Expressible in Plato with
    // a loop over At and an overflow test, but then every runtime owns a copy of the range
    // test and the profile decides it; one host call keeps the limits where the type's own
    // are. Witness: IntegerFromText("-12") == -12 and IntegerFromText("1.0") == 0.
    IntegerFromText(s: String): Integer;

    // The shortest text that reads back to this exact Number through NumberFromText, bit
    // for bit (the shortest round-trip digits, in the invariant culture): "0.1", "100",
    // "1E+17", "1E-05", "-0" (plain digits from 1E-04 up to below 1E+17, scientific
    // outside, as .NET writes the "R" form). NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are written "NaN", "Infinity" and
    // "-Infinity", and IsNumberText rejects all three, so only finite Numbers round-trip.
    // Not expressible in Plato: shortest round-trip digit generation needs the host's
    // algorithm (Ryu or Grisu with a fallback) and every runtime must pick the same digits.
    // Witness: NumberToShortestString(0.5) == "0.5" and NumberToShortestString(1e-5) == "1E-05".
    NumberToShortestString(x: Number): String;

    //==
    // Array — the five-function kernel.
    //
    // `Count` and `At` observe; `MapRange` is the ONLY constructor; `Reduce` is
    // the only sequential fold; `FlatMap` the only length-varying producer.
    // Every other array function in the previous contract is a reindexing of
    // MapRange, with a reference body in `primitives.library.plato`.
    //
    // Reduce and FlatMap cannot follow: neither is a reindexing of MapRange.
    // (An earlier note here said a body is a pure expression "with no loop".
    // That is false — bodies may use var/while/if and the List/Buffer builders,
    // per LIBRARIES.md ground rule 2. Only the no-recursion contract holds,
    // GLSL forbidding recursion outright. Whether these two are now expressible
    // and so belong in a library file per plato-378 has not been re-examined.)

    Count(xs: Array<$T>): Integer;
    At(xs: Array<$T>, n: Integer): $T;
    MapRange(n: Integer, f: Function1<Integer, $T>): Array<$T>;
    Reduce(xs: Array<$T>, acc: $U, f: Function2<$U, $T, $U>): $U;
    FlatMap(xs: Array<$T1>, f: Function1<$T1, Array<$T2>>): Array<$T2>;

    //==
    // Growable builder: unique type List<T>.
    //
    // Bodiless host signatures for the builder types declared in
    // `primitives.plato`. Without them no builder call site
    // resolves. The single-parameter observers and consumers — `Count`, `Freeze`
    // and `EmptyList` — are declared alongside the mutators. Each carries a type
    // variable that is fully determined by its one parameter
    // (`Count(xs: List<$T>)` fixes `$T` from its argument), so a call site can
    // infer it. The runtime (`PlatoList`/`PlatoBuffer`) implements all of them.

    // The number of elements accumulated so far. Observes; does not consume.
    Count(xs: List<$T>): Integer;

    // The element at the given index. Observes; does not consume.
    At(xs: List<$T>, n: Integer): $T;

    // Appends one element and returns the same builder. Rebind or chain.
    Add(xs: List<$T>, x: $T): List<$T>;

    // Appends every element of the array, in order, and returns the same
    // builder. Rebind or chain.
    AddRange(xs: List<$T>, values: Array<$T>): List<$T>;

    // Overwrites the element at the given index and returns the same builder.
    // Precondition: 0 <= i < Count.
    Set(xs: List<$T>, i: Integer, x: $T): List<$T>;

    // Zero-copy handoff of the accumulated elements to an immutable Array<$T>.
    // Consumes: the builder is invalidated and any later use throws.
    Freeze(xs: List<$T>): Array<$T>;

    // A fresh empty List whose element type matches the given array. Lets a
    // generic body obtain a builder where the element type is a type variable,
    // without naming a concrete type in `new List<...>()`.
    EmptyList(xs: Array<$T>): List<$T>;

    //==
    // Fixed-size builder: unique type Buffer<T>.

    // The number of slots. Observes; does not consume.
    Count(xs: Buffer<$T>): Integer;

    // The value written to the given slot. Observes; does not consume.
    At(xs: Buffer<$T>, n: Integer): $T;

    // Writes one slot and returns the same builder. Rebind or chain.
    // Precondition: 0 <= i < Count.
    Set(xs: Buffer<$T>, i: Integer, x: $T): Buffer<$T>;
